desc:
This underground lake measures nearly twelve yards from one wall to the other.
It is nearly perfectly round, and a cascade of shimmering water falls from above
and splashes into the lake. The water is pretty clear in the upper part of the
lake, but around two, three yards below the surface, it gets darker and dirtier,
making it impossible to see the bottom. A small, crystal clear stream rushes out
of a narrow tunnel to the east and flows on through a lower, but broader one to
the west.
name: The Underground Lake

desc:
The narrow tunnel becomes wider to the west, and the water rushes to that
direction. It is just some two feet deep and so clear that it nearly emits its
own, light blue light. The ground is smooth and mostly flat, whereas moisture
makes the walls shimmer slightly. To the east, the tunnel seems to have caved in
years ago, and to the south someone created carvings in the stone.
name: A Small Underground Stream

desc:
The tunnel is quite low while the walls, ceiling and floor have been polished by
the rushing water. From the ceiling, dark green algae hang into the water and
soft moss grows in spots at the upper part of the walls. Further west, the
tunnel gets even lower and finally, the rock touches the ripples and the fast
flowing stream continues underwater.
name: A Stream in a Low Tunnel

desc:
The rock is smoothly polished by the permanent current. Some low plants, growing
on the bottom of this stream, move their tendrils in the flow of the water, and
little, yellow dots shimmer on their long, flexible leaves. The tunnel gets
narrower but also much higher in the southern part.
name: An Underground Stream

desc:
While the walls on the sides could be touched by stretching the arms, the bottom
and ceiling of this stream are barely visible in the dark. Yet, it can be made
out that the floor seems to be covered with dark soil and an occasional plant
with large, nearly perfectly round leaves.
name: A Narrow and Deep Underground Stream

desc:
As the underground stream becomes narrow and very low, the current is very
strong in this place. In this current, it is hard to figure out where bottom,
ceiling or side are. The walls, however, are slick and napless, and only very
few, thin algae are able to grow on the bare rock. In the far end of the sight,
the tunnel gets even narrower, and the stream rushes into a black hole to the
south.
name: A Rushing Underground Stream

desc:
Grass emerges from the shelf to the west, but is cut off by dried and cracked
ground here. Only a few weeds have survived to keep growing, and only from
within the cracks along the ground. Most of the water from the rain probably
seeks its way into the cracks, giving these weeds enough nutrients to survive.
There are stones of various sizes scattered across the ground, with different
textures and colours. Some smaller pebbles cover the ground in sections to the
east. To the north, there is a steep ledge that leads down to a small dale.
name: Rocky Shelf

desc:
A small ledge begins to form in the centre of these dried grounds. It slowly
gains height as it climbs to the west, with a few rocks mixed into the soil. The
ground is dry and only few blades of grass have survived here, with three small
bushes standing on the eastern side of the ledge. The bushes are short, and
their leaves are crisp and dying.
name: Cracked Ledge

desc:
It looks as though a streambed had once passed through here, though now it is
diminished and only a slight trace of it along the ground can be noticed. Many
fine grains of sand cover most of the ground here along with tiny pebbles, a
mixture of various colours. The grass along the west and east side of the faded
streambed is bright green, as though it really flourished near the water at one
time long ago. Near the south end of the old streambed, young blades of grass
have grown, but it is not nearly as thick as the surrounding patches.
name: Diminished Streambed

desc:
The streambed appears to have once led here from the west, and after a slight
curve it headed in a southbound direction. There are several plants trying to
emerge from the dried and cracked soil of the dried-up bed, but it would appear
they are struggling to survive here. Some bright green grass has grown thick to
the north, where it looks like the plains expand.
name: Old Streambed

desc:
The ground is rough and cracked, with very small pebbles upon it in random piles
all over. The remains of a streambed can be noticed by the markings and patterns
along the ground, travelling east and west. A slight ledge forms in the south
and appears to grow higher as it continues westwards. The ledge to the north is
very tall, with some green grass noticeable on the top, continuing both east and
west.
name: Dried-up Streambed

desc:
The dale is half covered by small pebbles on the west side, and dry patches of
bare earth on the east. An occasional weed can be noticed, sprouting up from the
earth between the pebbles and looking very dry and unhealthy. To the north and
south are large walls of natural earth. This dale, long ago though, was most
likely a small and quiet stream, but has since dried up and remained bare.
name: Small Dale

desc:
A rocky protrusion has formed on the walls of the chasm, big enough to stand or
rest on with a small group, yet it is very uncomfortable. A few smaller bushes
grow on the edges, and some grass grows in the cracks of the wall. Every part of
the rock and bushes is damp, and small fungi grow all around. It seems to be
quite easy to climb down into the deep and dark chasm, but only a very skilled
climber would be able to find a way up without breaking his neck when trying.
name: A Protrusion in the Chasms Wall

desc:
The walls rise so high that only a small portion of the sky remains to be seen.
While some parts of the walls seem to offer some hold to plants and even smaller
trees, other parts are blank and steep, and not even a crack can be spotted. The
bottom of this chasm is moist, and large sections have been filled with dirty
water which stinks of decay and old mud. Some patches of black grass grow here,
and from the tenacious, black mud, a few broken bones of animals and travellers,
which have been so unlucky to slide into the chasm, stick out.
name: A Deep and Dark Chasm

desc:
The plains stretch from here, showing an assortment of grasses, wildflowers, and
small bushes of many different colours. A large stone stands almost in the
centre of the plain, light grey in colour, with a rough texture to it. Several
branches, all being very thin and splintered, are scattered around along the
ground.
name: Great Plains

desc:
The grass has grown quite fine here, bright green in colour and very thick in
appearance. The grass ends abruptly to the south, where there is a long drop
down to an old streambed below. The stump of an old tree stands firmly in the
earth still, with a few flowers growing out from around it. The plains appear to
expand to the east, and the ledge continues to the west.
name: Ledge of Fine Grass

desc:
Various stumps and boles of long dead trees are lying around here. On a few of
the stumps some scar-like markings can be seen, probably cut by a crude hatchet
or axe. Now some thick and dry brushwood dominates this area, covering
everything and choking back the trees' every attempt to regain their former
glory.
name: Remnants of a Forest

desc:
The ground here is barren and dark, being coloured by shades of black and brown.
Most of the ground is dry, so dry it appears like concrete and is filled with
small hollows and cracks. Small patches of dry grass and various half-dead
plants are scattered among the ground.
name: Sere Ground

desc:
Several weeds have sprouted from beneath the ground here, mixed in among long
blades of grass. The grass appears to be very crisp and dried. There are some
flowers growing along the western edge of the field, where a narrow dale courses
through the landscape. It looks like a dried-up streambed. The furrows in the
ground suggest that the water once flowed in from the east, perhaps creating a
small waterfall at this point.
name: At the Edge of a Narrow Dale

desc:
The field grows long blades of grass spreading out evenly across the ground.
Between them are patches of dried and bare ground. The grassy ledge, which is
almost unnoticeable until it is too late, travels along the western side of the
field, completely covered by tall lengths of grass and weeds. There are a few
stones littered about the field as well.
name: Grassy Ledge

desc:
The grass is fine here, bright green in colour, with only a few weeds noticeable
between the slender blades. Four trees have also grown here, spreading out
several feet from one another, all having long and thin branches. The leaves on
these trees are small, green, and oval in shape. The bark upon the trees appears
to be very smooth and light brown in colour. The grass gets taller as it expands
to the east, where there is also a small mound noticeable in the distance.
name: Slightly Wooded Meadow

desc:
The grassland here seems to continue to the south, though to the west, a few
trees stand barely discernible. The soil is broken up, with crisp blades of
grass growing in large clumps all over. Small mounds are rising out of the
earth, giving this landscape a distinct appearance.
name: Rough Grassland

desc:
The ground is covered by a thick bed of grass, with very few noticeable weeds.
To the east the grass becomes longer, though the growth is not as thick as it is
here. Some small pebbles are also noticeable along the east side of this grassy
area. This appears to be a ledge, since to the west and south there is a great
distance down to the ground below.
name: Grassy Ledge

desc:
The channel is completely dry, filled by tiny grains of sand and small pebbles.
It looks as though water had at one time flowed southwest from here, where the
sand slowly begins to fade and small spots of grass can be noticed. On one side
of the dried-up channel stands a tall tree, coated by a grey-coloured bark. A
few flowers have sprouted up from the earth on both sides of the sandy bed
together with several stones. A large hill stands to the east, but due to the
erosion over the years, it is impossible to reach it from this side.
name: Dried-up Channel

desc:
The barren, sandy landscape here is dominated by a dried, meandering channel,
which still bears visible marks of once flowing water. Pebbles along the dry
valley are round, as the once gushing water has curved the edges from all
stones. Small bushes have surrounded the channel and dried there in the past,
leaving only empty skeletal branches behind. The channel continues to both the
north and the south.
name: Dead Channel

desc:
This deep, dry basin seems completely lifeless. The ground is dry and extremely
hard-surfaced, coloured with shades of black and brown. The brinks of this bowl
do not rise very steeply. Along the northern edge of the old pool huge logs and
small boulders can be noticed, perhaps the remains of an ancient pier.
name: Extinct Lake

desc:
Short, stunted grass covers this area into austere embrace. Even the land is
arid and barren, with its grass growing dark green. Some holes of various small
rodents can be seen all around the landscape, and almost non-existing trails
connect the burrows to each other. There are some old fences piled up along the
northeast side of the plain, and some large boulders stand in the southeastern
parts.
name: Bare Plain

desc:
The slightly rolling country here is filled with stunted hummocks and tussocks.
Some brushwood, mainly heather and some various herbs grow here. The ground
appears pretty dry, while the growth is strong and stable. A couple of large
rocks and circular-shaped stones are scattered around on the ground. To the
south, a slight rise in the earth can be noticed.
name: Stunted Hummocks

desc:
In the centre of the plains is a large knoll, emerged slightly from the earth.
Grass has fully covered the knoll, along with some white flowers that have grown
upon it. There are large stones at the southern end, which were probably some
type of a marker long ago, but have since crumbled and toppled over into a large
pile of debris. Long-stemmed wildflowers and tall blades of grass cover the
largest portion of debris, making it almost unnoticeable.
name: Steep Knoll

desc:
The flat field here consists of extremely dry ground. Some remains of fences
built long ago, made of some huge, dry logs, can still be seen around. Now their
skeletal forms are the sole guard of this long abandoned area. Some half-buried
bones are the only other reference to what this land might have formerly been
used for.
name: Ancient Lea

desc:
The slightly rolling country has suffered badly from continuous erosion, caused
by aridity, heat and time. The pebbly and sandy ground here grows only some weak
grass but incredibly lush bushes, which reveal some of the landscapes former
fertility. Some ancient formations of stone can be seen around, half buried into
the sand and bush growth.
name: Lush Bushes

desc:
The landscape here is barren, growing weak grass and various thorny bushes. The
ground is mostly composed of sand and pebble instead of soil. Some man-sized
boulders are lying here, half buried in the sand, and branches of thorny growth
are rising out from their sides. To the west, the scenery rises slightly while
it becomes more rocky.
name: Thorny Bushes

desc:
This part of the cavern is filled with smoke and other strong aromas floating in
the air. The stone floor is covered with a thick and soft carpet, which is
dirtied by all possible blemishes. Pieces of crude furniture, some wrecked and
some undamaged, share the floor space in disarray. Above a fireplace in the
corner, the cavern ceiling seems to disappear out of sight.
name: Smelly Chamber

desc:
This dark cavern opens as wide as high, enclosing all of the surroundings to
deep shadows. The basement rock along the ground is flooded with all sorts of
rubbish and food leftovers, which could be fresh marks of the inhabitants. Some
light can be seen further into the darkness. A small stream of water flows
onwards along the ground, only to disappear into a small hole.
name: Smelly Chamber

desc:
The threshold is long, though narrow, and leading toward a building that lies to
the north, with an oaken door marking its entrance. Thick, dark wood was used to
create the threshold, and a glossy finish was placed on it. The ceiling was
created with the same kind of wood, but at the southern end of it, there is a
red banner that dangles down. The ground is bare of any debris, materials, or
even grass, with only dry earth to walk over. The threshold is large enough so
that it appears to block any sunlight or rough weather from entering.
name: Threshold to a Shelter

desc:
This shelter was obviously reconstructed over time from its original build, as
some of the wood used for the walls is new compared to the rest. It has a glossy
coating upon it, while the old portions appear to have started to splinter due
to age. The western part of the ceiling is solid wood as well, while the rest is
covered with a thick tarp along one side of the shelter. Large wooden beams with
some engravings support the solid part of the roof, but the other side lacks
them. Especially the north-eastern portion of the roof looks extremely aged and
buckled. Large sheets of wood cover the floor, with an old rug lying upon them.
name: A Reconstructed Shelter

desc:
This roof covers a very old structure of some kind, even though the boards are
quite decayed and splintered in several different places. On the southeastern
side of the roof here, a dark-coloured tarp can be noticed, probably tied there
to cover a gaping hole. The roof steeply slants up to the west, while the
northern part seems easier to reach. Looking down from the roof, a rocky dale
runs to the south from this building.
name: On a Decaying Roof

desc:
The boards used for the roof here are very old, cracked in several places, and
already well into a decaying state. The roof rises up on a high slant to the
west, and would be too steep to climb to the other side. The boards along the
upper portion of that slant are even more decayed than those right here. The
roof offers a view of the surrounding dale but there is no visibility to the
fields above. A ladder is set against the northern wall of the dale, leading
upwards to a grassy ledge.
name: On a Decaying Roof

desc:
The growth of tall grass dominates the flat ground here. A small spring gushes
here, forming a small stream which then flows rapidly to the west, giving some
much needed moisture to all vegetation. Some blooming plants colour the land
which surrounds the tiny source of the brook. This paradisiacal oasis does not
seem to have any larger plants though.
name: Tall Grass

desc:
A short but strong grassbed covers the ground here. The surroundings are painted
in various shades of green. A constant wind may have forced most of the stalks
of grass to bend low in this open area. Some small plants have grown at random
spots here and there, wherever they could manage to find shelter against the
weather.
name: Short Grass

desc:
Short, strong grass covers the ground here. Some ancient stumps and boles have
broken through the grassbed, revealing the remains of some destroyed forest. A
single tree is still remaining, raising its naked trunk up to the heights. It
may have stood here branchless and leafless for ages, but still offers some
shelter to various small animals such as birds and insects.
name: Lone Tree in the Plains

desc:
Some stunted and slow-growing bushes rule the landscape here. Weak grass and
some especially strong plants grow below the bushes. The undergrowth is formed
mostly of different waxy-leafed herbs, which can accept this barren plain as
their substrate.
name: Stunted Plain

desc:
Small bushes have spread their growth all around this area, leaving all of the
grass as a weak minority which is forced to fight for its existence. The
alteration of different ground types is clearly visible here, when the lush
steppes, the arid field and the scrubby plains meet. Only a few weeds appear to
stand out, mainly due to their dark colour.
name: Small Bushes

desc:
Various bushes grow here, rising knee-high and covering the dry ground below
them. The brush has long and slender branches, extending out from the earth. A
few thorns which seem to be rather sharp and very short in length can be noticed
upon these branches.
name: Thorny Brush

desc:
In the air here, there flows a gentle fragrance of wood and resin, generated by
low, woody shrubs covering the ground. Where bushes and twigs have lost their
grasp on the land, dirt and grass cover the earthy ground, here and there
adjourned by clusters of dandelions and moss. Chickweed seems to grow
everywhere.
name: Rosiny Bushes

desc:
Short but wide shrubs nestle to each other, forming a dense, green and brown
living carpet which burdens movement. Only at a few spots, the carpet opens for
some kind of natural pathways paved with nettles, thistles and other small
plants. The fragrance of different herbs can be smelled in the air, mingled with
a faint, yet sharp stench.
name: Squat Bushes

desc:
Thick and strong brush covers the area, growing in all shapes and sizes. Nearly
hidden by the brushwood, a soft slope eases down into a vague sink in the land,
barely noticeable for an inattentive observer. Many tiny rills and small holes
in the surrounding ground yet indicate that the water from rainfalls steadily
flows into the dip, eroding the vicinity and slowly but steadily filling it.
name: Shallow Dip in the Brush

desc:
The field is covered with thin, woody grass. A few flowers manage to survive
while being at a permanent strife for survival. Rocks lie here and there on the
ground, and close to most of them, bushes and higher grass grow. The soil is
hard and poor, and dust can be felt in the air.
name: Scarce Grassland

desc:
The landscape here is dominated by wildly sprawling shrubs and brush. On the
wind-beaten ground, various rocks are uncovered, protruding through the thin
layer of soil. The air is light, enriched by the spicy smell of the bushes which
nearly conceals the elusive scent of herbs and dirt carried along by the wind.
name: Wild Brush

desc:
The dry lands are filled with golden grass, grasping through the thin layer of
soil on the stony ground with their stems, leaving it cracked. At some places
the grass grows to the height of a fully grown man's waist, and yet, at in other
places it has lost the battle against the hard ground, leaving it barren and
only covered with a few patches of moss.
name: Grassy, Cracked Ground

desc:
Among fields of grass in tones of gold and yellow, a tiny hill arises,
overlooking the vicinity. Although being only small in size, the hill is still
noticeable compared to the flat surrounding ground. Green grass and moss cover
it, and a few barren spots can be seen on it. Flowers of all colours grow
everywhere, making this a good landmark for a traveller.
name: A Tiny Hill

desc:
The rank ground seems to have hardened over time here. Fragile stems of grass in
gold and yellow and cabbages in all tones of brown and green cover it. Gravel,
rocks and hard chunks of soil form the surface between the strays of grass.
Small patches of moss clutch at the earth, slowly easing the ground again.
name: A Dry Field

desc:
Large patches of golden grass is growing here, now and then being interrupted by
solitary and small clusters of trees. The shimmering grass predominates the
landscape as the soil seems to be somewhat unyielding, but compared to what can
be seen to the south, it would do well for any farmer willing to bestow it.
name: Field of Grass

desc:
Tall and proud grass grows here in abundance, dominating the ground and rising
to the waist of a man, confident in its becoming. Its edges are pointy, tickling
a wanderer with every move, while small plants of many different kinds grow
among it. A few rocks lie around, being a disruption of the otherwise perfectly
level landscape.
name: Rich Grass

desc:
A low ledge cuts through the land. Tall and golden grass grows throughout the
area, bathing the surrounding ground in gold and green. Its cause is uncertain,
but it has left a glaring scar in the fertile landscape, and grass and small
plants can only cover the edge. Rocks and gravel have tumbled down and lie in a
stony field to the north below the ledge.
name: At a Ledge

desc:
The soil here has a genuine richness that would make any attempt at farming a
success. The grass of these fields, uninhibited by poor soil or lacklustre
weather, have covered the entire landscape with their golden threads, growing
tall and strong. Among them, other weeds can be spotted only very rarely, and
wherever they strive for survival, the grass seems to overwhelm it.
name: Thriving Grass

desc:
The grass here sparkles with an impressive variety of colours. While only a few
fully green straws can be seen, there are all shades and sizes of golden,
yellow, brown, grey and orange grass. In the setting sun, this field of colours
would have one face, while in the rising sun, an entirely different one would be
visible. Downfall is obviously plentiful to feed this variety of plants.
name: Lush Grassland

desc:
To the south, the way is blocked by a wide ledge, crossing through the fields.
In the shadows beneath, there it lie rocks and gravel as if hurled from the edge
above. Traces of animal activity can be seen all along the wall as this location
is perfect for protection from the path of the sun in the south. A few dark
spots can be seen along the rock of the ledge.
name: Below a Ledge

desc:
Small dunes and some bumps cross through this area, mostly in the southern part
of it. On the higher parts of the ground, it seems to be drier. Only some golden
grass grows there that has partially turned grey and brown. In the lower and
wetter areas, the grass grows stronger with a more luscious tone, and large
shrubs spread their branches wide and high.
name: Uneven Plains

desc:
A thin layer of top-soil tries to cover the ground here, but in some places, it
has been eroded and reveals a thick layer of granite. Grass can only be seen in
a few places among large areas of ling, and a tiny path leads northwards sloping
between a few hills. Rocks of all shapes and sizes rest upon the path from their
brief fall down the nearby elevations.
name: Rocky Ground

desc:
The flat surface of a steep cliff rises high to the north, looming over the
lower, grass-covered ground. Many flowers with a short stem and bulbous,
triangular blossom bloom here for most of the year, painting the dull landscape
in tones of violet, blue, pink and white. Among them, where the flowers grow
densest, there rests an old, mostly weathered stone with inscriptions on it.
name: South of a Steep Cliff

desc:
The evident lack of nutrients has left the shrubs weak and twisted at this
place. On the ground, more rocks than soil can be seen, and the fine layer of
dust that lies atop shifts in occasional breezes. A low, lonely tree can be seen
on a small incline. Large rocks surround it in a nearly perfect semicircular
shape as if specifically placed there, and surprisingly dense bushes grow close
by.
name: Twisted Brush
